decision: accept bounded full-body presentation preview and continuous left-hand return; keep Aim shouldering and fine contact limitations explicit
reviewer_role: hero pose author reviewing root-owned native capture; root also performs independent integration/visual review

actual_review.method: Viewed all 13 full-resolution named originals, all 135 consecutive hero-viewport crops in five labeled sheets, and 8 full-resolution return-boundary originals. Cropping/resizing is an analysis derivative; originals remain untouched.

findings.result: Both hands remain associated with the firearm in the visible hold; Aim blends to a modestly raised/reoriented chest-level stance. No detached hand is apparent at the captured viewport scale. Stock/cheek contact and sight-to-eye alignment are not established.

Left hand visibly releases into the throw follow-through and continuously approaches the foregrip during return. Frames49/50 show the completed support pose without a visibility replacement. Right hand retains the gun.
Open palm is lower than Q/X in the named still. The arm withdraws continuously to the foregrip; frames73/74 show the completion. No on-screen hand removal is used.
Both hands stay on the firearm with a small torso brace. Feet remain planted. This preview shows the brace only; it does not depict an actual dash displacement.

Raised palm remains open during the longer emphasis, then closes/returns continuously. Frames119–122 preserve the support hand through return completion. C/Q/X gestures remain visually similar at the full-body viewport scale; no full-body projectile or damage effect is present in this preview.

Advancing frames keep both feet on the same platform. The visible cape/garment stays continuous without a new gross separation around the arms. Back still retains quiver removal. Hidden-side contact during moving gestures and close-up cloth intersections are not fully resolved by this view.
Actual SURYA and the accepted first-person hand poses render in the separate studio view. Q open hand and X local charge rings are visible; no match authority or world effects are implied.
The full figure remains visible at960×540 and150% UI scale, but its reduced pixel height prevents detailed finger or facial-art acceptance.

The first four film originals show the truthful Preparing Rama’s studio message after switching back from first-person mode. Hero visibility begins at4. The original nine-second film includes this transition.

prior_numeric_evidence.scope: Imported bone continuity, reachable wrists, accepted fingertip-skin retention and exact lower-body preservation; not a new absolute collision/contact oracle.

remaining_limits: Aim needs a future shouldering/cheek/eye-line pass before finished full-body ADS acceptance.
E is an in-place upper-body brace; preview poses do not establish full-body tactical locomotion or gameplay ability animation.
Full-body Q/C/X share restrained open-palm language; stronger silhouette distinction, unseen-side cloth clearance and close-up skin/weapon contact remain future art work.
The pre-existing first-person one-frame support-grip restoration remains documented in finish2; this full-body preview work does not change that module.

Small viewport size and procedural/borrowed grip shaping limit anatomy judgments. No ordinary OS-input, human game-feel, audio listening, consumer-GPU performance or online claim comes from this scripted software-rendered preview.
work_done: Read-only native source/report inspection, SHA-256/dimension checks and visual inspection. Wrote review documents and labeled crop sheets only; no runtime edit, test rerun, import or render.
